_note: Baseline for the behavioural tier. UNMEASURED: no graded run has been performed, because the graded tier needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and that secret is a separate human action (issue #171). Every statistic below is null on purpose. Seeding it with a plausible number would give #173's regression alarm something to compare against that nobody measured, which is the failure mode CLAUDE.md's readout section spends a page on: reporting health from absent evidence. The shape is aggregate_benchmark.py's output so a real run drops straight in.
comparability: A BASELINE IS ONLY COMPARABLE AGAINST RUNS OF THE SAME MODEL. metadata.executor_model and metadata.analyzer_model below record which model produced these numbers; the Aggregate step in skills-eval.yml stamps them from what the runner observed on the wire, because the `model` dispatch input is blank on any run that took the CLI default and aggregate_benchmark.py otherwise writes the literal string "<model-name>" (issue #203). Compare a run against this baseline only when those fields match. A model change moves the pass rate for reasons that have nothing to do with the skills, and #173's regression alarm reading a mismatched pair would report a skill regression that is really a model upgrade — attributing the delta to the wrong cause. When the models differ, the right move is to re-seed the baseline on the new model, not to interpret the delta.
how_to_seed: 1. Add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as a repository secret.
2. Run the 'Skills eval (behavioural)' workflow via workflow_dispatch with runs=3. Three runs is the minimum that yields a stddev worth reading.
3. Download the behavioural-benchmark artifact and commit its benchmark.json over this file.
4. Read the stddev before trusting the mean. Per evals/README.md a wide-variance case is a defect in the case, not a finding about the skill — fix the case before it becomes a baseline.

5. Check that metadata.executor_model is a real model name and not null. A null means no model could be read off the event streams, and a baseline that cannot name its model cannot be compared against anything later.
